acceptance_criteria.given: an agent's submission through the submit route of a document with three local tasks declaring no `files` and no `depends_on`
acceptance_criteria.then: `warnings` holds one entry naming all three task keys and saying to add `files` and chain with `depends_on`; fails before, when `warnings` is empty

acceptance_criteria.given: two local tasks where one declares `files` and one does not, submitted through the route
acceptance_criteria.then: the warning names only the one without `files`

acceptance_criteria.given: an otherwise complete document whose tasks trigger the warning, submitted through the route, and separately a document with two declared, unordered, overlapping tasks
acceptance_criteria.then: `blocking` is empty and `ready_to_propose` is true for the first, and the second still returns its `unordered_file_overlap` entry unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: (a) a document with one local task and no `files`, (b) one local task without `files` plus one imported entry, (c) three local tasks all declaring `files`, each submitted through the route

design: Decisions. (1) The warning is a sibling of `overlap_warnings`, not a change to it: that function's contract ("tasks declaring no files are never named") is tested in hub/tests/test_spec_task_files.py and stays true; the new function covers the case it deliberately skips. (2) One Finding per submission listing all offending tasks, not one per task, so a planner that skipped the step gets one message to act on, not N. (3) Threshold is two LOCAL tasks (`from_ is None`): with one task there is nothing to order, so a warning would be noise a planner learns to ignore. An empty `files` list counts as undeclared, as `overlap_warnings` already treats it (`t.files` falsy). (4) It is advisory and stays out of `check`, so approval is never held up by a task whose files the planner genuinely cannot predict; the cost of a false positive is one line of text. (5) Test through the route because F190-style failures pass the unit and cannot fire: the response shape is built in agent_actions.py:1779 from `SaveResult.warnings`. ACCEPTANCE DRIVE (operator's, after merge, on a fresh Hub): a Haiku planner is asked to draft a slice with several tasks over one file and skips `files`. PASS: its submit response contains the undeclared-files warning naming those tasks. FAIL: `warnings` is empty for that submission. Reviewer: aw-reviewer.

limits: Proposed coverage only: the route tests are derived from the acceptance criteria and have not been run. Whether a real Haiku planner acts on the warning is the operator's acceptance drive; a passing suite does not show it.

problem: Slice 1/1b taught every planner to list each task's `files` and chain tasks that share a path, and made the submission warn when two DECLARED tasks overlap (`spec_completeness.overlap_warnings`, `unordered_file_overlap`). A re-drive with a real Haiku planner (scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md F509) followed the teaching in one of two runs. The other wrote three tasks editing one file with no `files` and no `depends_on`; the submission said nothing, because `overlap_warnings` considers only tasks that declare files (`declared = [t for t in payload.tasks if t.from_ is None and t.files]`). The planner that skips the step is the one the overlap check cannot see, so the safety net has a hole exactly where it is needed. Teaching text is read once and ignored; a response the planner receives on every submission is read.

requirements.statement: When a submitted document declares two or more local tasks and at least one of them declares no `files` (absent or empty), the submit response carries one warning, in the same `warnings` list as `unordered_file_overlap`, that names every such task by key and states that each should list the paths it will edit in `files` and that tasks sharing a path must be chained with `depends_on`.

The undeclared-files warning never blocks: for a document that is otherwise complete, `blocking` stays empty and `ready_to_propose` stays true with or without the warning, and the existing `unordered_file_overlap` warnings are produced exactly as before.

No undeclared-files warning is produced for a document with fewer than two local tasks (imported entries do not count toward the two, and are never named), nor for one whose every local task declares `files`.

in_scope: One new advisory warning in the submit response, produced beside `overlap_warnings` in hub/hub/spec_completeness.py and carried by the same `SaveResult.warnings` list (hub/hub/spec_service.py:294) to the agent's response (hub/hub/api/v1/agent_actions.py:1779)
A warning that names every local task without `files` and says what to add
non_goals: Blocking: `ready_to_propose` and `blocking` are unchanged, as for `unordered_file_overlap`
Inferring a task's files in the Hub
Warning a one-task document, or a document whose local tasks all declare files
Counting imported entries (`from`) either as tasks that should declare files or toward the two-task threshold
Any database migration, or any change that needs this Hub restarted while the slice is built
Rewording the planner's duty text or the tool descriptions (slice 1b's job); if a task changes tool text anyway, the Claude context snapshot must be regenerated

summary: A planner that writes several tasks and declares `files` on none (or only some) of them is told so by the submit response, with the tasks named and the fix stated, instead of being silently accepted.

tasks.description: Files: hub/hub/spec_completeness.py, hub/hub/spec_service.py, and a new hub/tests/test_spec_undeclared_files_warning.py. Add a function beside `overlap_warnings` returning at most one Finding (area 'tasks') per the three requirements, and append its result to the `warnings` list built at spec_service.py:294. Do not add it to `check`. Tests at the submit route as an agent's submission (use the route-level pattern of hub/tests/test_spec_roadmaps.py), not only the unit; each must fail before the change. Include a check that hub/hub/migrations/versions is unchanged from master. Before completing run the WHOLE hub suite (`py -3.11 -m pytest tests/ -q -n 4` from hub/), then `black --check --target-version py311` and `ruff check` on `src/ hub/ tests/`. If you changed any tool or duty text, regenerate the snapshot with AW_UPDATE_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT=1 (hub/tests/test_copilot_context_split.py) and say so.
